expectations.text: Acknowledges the coupling between subsystems explicitly
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states: 'You're facing a classic tightly-coupled system where subsystems have circular dependencies.' Problem Context section lists the key couplings: 'Attitude affects which solar panels see the sun', 'Power availability affects whether heaters can run', etc.

expectations.text: Proposes architectural pattern to manage cross-cutting concerns (e.g., central state, publish-subscribe, event-driven)
expectations.evidence: Response proposes 'unidirectional data flow' pattern with computation order within each timestep: 'Break the circular dependencies by establishing a computation order.' Defines sequential update pattern: Orbital → Attitude → Power → Thermal. Also mentions shared state object approach.

expectations.text: Identifies subsystems: Attitude Dynamics, Power System, Thermal System, Orbital/Environmental (sun position, eclipse)
expectations.evidence: Response identifies required subsystems: (1) Attitude Subsystem (owns quaternion, angular velocity, reaction wheels, magnetorquers), (2) Power Subsystem (owns battery SOC, solar panel state, power budget), (3) Thermal Subsystem (owns component temperatures, heater states), (4) Orbital Mechanics/Environment (computes sun vector, eclipse state, magnetic field).

expectations.text: Defines clear data flow showing how attitude affects power which affects thermal
expectations.evidence: Data flow diagram shows: 'Orbital Mechanics → Attitude Control (uses attitude from t-1, updates state) → Power Generation (uses updated attitude, computes sun angles on panels) → Thermal Management (uses power availability, decides heater states).' Clear sequential chain demonstrating the coupling.

expectations.text: Suggests implementation strategy with stubbed dependencies to enable independent development
expectations.evidence: While the response mentions 'Build incrementally' and suggests starting with one subsystem at a time, it does not explicitly recommend stubbing dependencies. The implementation section focuses on the integration pattern but doesn't provide concrete guidance on how to develop subsystems independently with mocked inputs.

expectations.text: Recommends starting with simplified assumptions (e.g., constant sun angle) before adding full complexity
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Start with fixed attitude (sun-pointing), build power subsystem, verify battery charge/discharge, close the loop.' Recommends beginning with simplified cases: 'Acceptance of one-timestep lag' for most couplings to simplify implementation before adding tighter coupling if needed.
